question.questionText: The kids were very hungry. They______ around in the garden all afternoon.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank requires a verb tense that shows an action that happened before another action in the past. The sentence 'The kids were very hungry. They______ around in the garden all afternoon.' describes two past actions: the kids were hungry (past simple), and before that, they had been running (past perfect continuous). The past perfect continuous tense ('had been running') is used to show that an action (running) was happening over a period of time before another action in the past (being hungry).
  • had been running (verb phrase): Past perfect continuous tense, used to show an action that was ongoing in the past before another past action.
  • will has been running (verb phrase): Incorrect tense formation. 'Will' is used for future, and 'has been' is present perfect. They cannot be combined this way.
  • has been running (verb phrase): Present perfect continuous tense, used for actions that started in the past and continue to the present. Not suitable here because the context is in the past.
  • hasn’t been running (verb phrase): Negative form of present perfect continuous. Incorrect tense and meaning for this context.
Related structure or vocabulary: Past perfect continuous tense: S + had been + V-ing, used to show an action that was happening over a period of time before another action in the past.
